newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Dah Sing Financial unit HK$ FRCD raised.
newsitem.headline: Dah Sing Financial unit HK$ FRCD raised.

text.p: Dah Sing Bank's three-year floating rate certificates of deposit issue has been raised to HK$1.5 billion from HK$1.2 billion because of oversubscription, bookrunner HSBC Markets said on Wednesday.
Dah Sing Bank is a unit of Dah Sing Financial Holdings Ltd.
The certificates were priced at par to float at 40 basis points over the three-month Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate. With fees, the all-in return for top-tier managers is 56 basis points.
Application has been made to the Hong Kong Monetary Authority to accept the issue as eligible for its Liquidity Adjustment Facility, or discount window.
Dah Sing Bank is rated A-minus by European rating agency IBCA.
Arrangers, with HK$161 million each, are China Development Finance Co (Hong Kong), Commerz (East Asia), HSBC Markets, United Overseas Bank and Westpac Banking Corp.

Senior co-lead managers are DKB Asia, with HK$150 million, Nippon Credit International (HK) and Standard Chartered Bank, each with HK$100 million, and Banca Commerciale Italiana's Hong Kong branch and Hang Seng Bank, each with HK$80 million.
Co-lead manager Ka Wah Bank committed to HK$50 million.
Senior managers are ING Bank's Hong Kong branch, with HK$45 million, and Asia Commercial Bank, China Construction Bank's Hong Kong branch and Royal Bank of Scotland, each with HK$30 million.
Signing is set for December 9. The payment date is December 16.
